attempts.outcome: The complete 47-target disposition contains 38 export objects on 40 faces and nine absent objects. Explicit source pointers distinguish 40 pre-firing vessel stamps, six low-fired tags from secondary contexts and one unbaked jar stopper. Two targets gain identified primary drawings and individual locus, lot and item keys: H-1745 from Period 3C sump-pit fill, and H-1734 from Trench 10W fill. The seven-object sealing class fails the prespecified minimum of ten independent groups, so no classifier or new sign meaning was scored. Fifty author integrity and replay checks pass.

On rectangular seals None means no motif: 8 of 8 sampled faces carry one row of signs and nothing else (motif-present share 0, 95% interval 0 to 0.37). On square seals None does not: 6 of 12 sampled faces are broken or worn where a motif would be, 5 of the 6 readable faces carry signs only and 1 shows a device. The placeholder - on square seals covers 5 fragments or worn faces in 8 and one seal with a large animal (M-1005); - on seals without a shape code covers 4 fragments in 4; the two ? and Unknown faces are unreadable. All 4 control crops with a named motif show one. Mapping v1 keeps None as an asserted absence only on rectangular seals (361 objects) and marks the other 97 None seal objects and every placeholder as unknown, which lowers seal motif coverage from 2,110 of 2,239 objects (94.2%) under the 12 October inventory rule to 2,013 (89.9%).

Calibration: of 757 personal donor occurrences in Lüders's list, 42 (5.5%) carry strictly marked asterism names and 57 (7.5%) under the broad marking; they use 12 or 16 of 25 asterism labels, Puṣya supplies 19, and their normalised entropy (0.775, 0.835) is below that of matched non-asterism name elements (median 0.993), which are open (Chao1 2,282). Two independent markings agree with kappa 0.97. Discovery half of seed 2026-10-21-birth-star-names (666 seal legends): the direction note's N1 and N3 fail as written (prefix-plus-run compounds have 60 types and Chao1 186; no modifier distinguishes three bases); N2 is retired because the calibrated birth-star class itself is less even than matched open vocabulary. Fish runs without their stroke prefix have 33 types and Chao1 38.6, match the broad Brahmi profile at 57 occurrences, keep their four commonest forms at 62-75% across Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Lothal and Dholavira, and are independent of the following sign (p = 0.36); runs of other sign families are as closed, and 35.6% of legends carry a fish run against 5.5-7.5% asterism names among Brahmi donors. Five predictions, the scorer and the reference data were frozen through bench shots at 2026-10-21T03:36Z for fresh seals only; C-0013 stands at 0.03. The confirmation half was not read.

Rows for every printed entry: CISI 1 1,543, CISI 2 2,139 (with the pilot's 327). 2,602 of 3,680 entries join one Lipi family; among them museum number 226 to 2,373, holding institution 226 to 2,560, FC number 0 to 2,599, excavation 2,459 to 2,483. Corpus museum-number coverage, combined with earlier sources, 340 (7.2%) to 2,450 (52.2%) counting uncertain digits, 2,079 (44.3%) with a definite number, 1,994 (42.5%) with a bracket-free cell. CISI 1: 98.6% cell agreement, all 112 disagreements adjudicated, 7 definite wrong readings per reader, 5 cells bracketed. CISI 2: 65.3% agreement; 256 disagreements in three blocks adjudicated (54 and 29 definite wrong readings in 1,205 cells), the other 2,870 kept as the union of both readings (Amendment 2). Predictions: FC = 2000 + Mackay No. or 1000 + Marshall No. for 560 of 573 Mohenjo-daro entries (97.7%, threshold 95%); Lipi's Harappa registration extensions equal the FC tail for 221 of 226 scorable (80.1% to 97.8%, threshold 80%); CISI 1 agreement 98.6% against the pilot's 90.5%.

The basic data (printed pp. 434-447, PDF 469-482) has five columns: CISI number, FC concordance number, excavation number, museum and registration numbers, photograph sources; it prints no findspot, depth, material or dimensions, and CISI 1 (p. 366) has the same columns. The scan's catalogue page order holds at both ends (printed = PDF - 35; 418 of 447 headers confirm it). All 327 entries M-621 to M-947 were transcribed and read twice by independent AI readers: cell agreement 90.5% (CISI number 100%, FC 92.7%, excavation 91.4%, museum 85.6%, photographs 82.6%); of 156 disagreements 48 were decided from the page and 108 were not; 119 of 1,635 final cells stay bracketed. Sampled first-pass error rate (33 rows): excavation 3.0% (1/33), FC 6.1%, museum 0%, all cells 1.8% (up to 4.2% counting undecidable cells); full comparison: first-pass errors 0.2% of cells, up to 6.2%. 283 entries join one Lipi family each, 44 have none. Museum number for the joined objects 26.1% to 97.5% (202 objects gained, 179 without an uncertain digit); corpus museum coverage 5.8% to 10.1% (274 to 476 objects); holding institution supplied for all 283 (added for 209) and FC number for all 283. Lipi excavation-idno equals the printed number for 40 objects and is the printed number plus the FC number without its first digit for 182, and those digits are the excavator's catalogue number (FC = 1000 + Marshall 1931 No. or 2000 + Mackay 1938 No. for 216 of 219 checkable objects); two pairs of records are crossed between Lipi and CISI 2, and plate measurements show CISI 2's basic data to be the source in error; two differ where the page confirms CISI 2. Museum numbers agree with the older export for all 71 comparable objects. Projected agent time for the rest: about 2.8 h for CISI 2 (1,760 entries) and 2.4 h for CISI 1 (1,533), at 5.7 s per entry. Independently verified on 13 October; four rights redactions and three count corrections applied (REVIEW-CHANGES.md).

Audited the focal paper and extracted nine published phase summaries at five comparison sites. Bahola's winter share rises by 10.42 percentage points and its summer share falls by 15.36 points between Late Harappan and PGW assemblages. Reconstructed cereal-denominator millet figures of 54.05% and 71.37%. The focal paper's three reported crop date ranges predate a 1200 BCE PGW reference; its complete supplement and layer-phase joins remain uninspected. Developed three conjectures: practical transmission through local networks, agricultural knowledge crossing into Indo-Aryan speech communities, and a long-shot diagnostic Vedic operation with an Indus-period ancestor. Starting credences are 0.65, 0.50 and 0.20, explicitly subjective. A horsegram case joins published botanical and lexical proposals while preserving multiple-domestication and alternate-route explanations. Established language genealogy, scholarly models and new hypotheses are recorded separately; no historical prediction is confirmed.

Sixteen needed senses of nine words were coded from the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary on the 20 tips of the Kolipakam 2018 MCC tree (root 4,433 years). 'Star' lies in entry 4876 (miṉ 'to shine'), separate from 4885 (mīn 'fish'), and is attested in Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Kota, Toda, Gondi, Kurukh and Malto. Its Mk1 maximum-likelihood root probability is 0.524 and North Dravidian node probability 0.681; parsimony places it absent at the root. The needed meanings reach the root in 7 of 14 comparable cases against a reference mean of 0.54 (p = 1/10001). P1, P2 and P3 pass; the kill condition fails; the frozen rule gives credence 0.35. Posterior trees give 0.520 (89% above 0.5); a star form homophonous with mīn gives 0.41 at the root and 0.22 at the North node; DravLex fieldwork forms give 0.001. DEDR records no banyan sense for vaṭam, no squirrel sense for piḷḷai and no Murukan sense for vēḷ. Review credence 0.20.

Discovery, 99 period-labelled seals in seven frames outside Mound F's stratified seals: union closing stock (DK-G 12 signs plus Harappa 405, 154, 595) closes 0.71 early and 0.73 late; no drift test reaches p 0.05 (openings 0.56, closings 0.59, length 0.51, inventory 0.82, variants 0.084); rectangular seals 0.09 to 0.29 (p 0.015). Credence 0.35 to 0.40 before the freeze. Confirmation, 173 Mound F seals in six trench frames, one read 21 s after the hashed freeze: P1 pass (stock share late minus early -0.044, 0.848 to 0.805, 90% interval -0.190 to 0.102), P2 pass (0.848), P3 no drift (openings z 0.09, p 0.39), P4 drift (variants z 5.94, p 0.0001, Holm 0.0006), P5 drift (length r 0.273, two-sided p 0.003, Holm 0.012; 4.04, 4.77, 5.31 signs by third), P6 drift (inventory z 3.73, p 0.0016, Holm 0.008), P7 no drift (closings p 0.70), PC pass (rectangular r 0.230, p 0.0017). Drift with Holm p below 0.05 in P4-P6 kills C-0010 at 0.02 (effects alone 0.32). Whole-mound permutation, depth clock, DK-G stock alone and complete legends alone give the same outcomes; variant drift depends on Trench I (p 0.16 without it). Independent script reproduces population, shares, length r 0.2725 (p 0.0032) and inventory 42.52 (p 0.0012). Post-outcome (exploratory): drift holds with format fixed (0.0005, 0.0029, 0.0052) and on square seals alone (0.0006, 0.009, 0.037); interior signs 2.0, 2.9, 3.3; 806 (0/4/8 legends by third), 817 (0/7/7), 233 (1/5/8) arrive, 390 (7/3/2) and 741 fade; interior signs become less Mohenjo-daro-like (r -0.25, p 0.004).

Built object- and site-linked corpora: Indo-Aryan seals and sealings from Basarh and Bhita (556 records, 245 eligible distinct legends at sign level, 30 at word level), Tamil-Brahmi seals, rings and coins (31 records, 23 and 7), Ur III Sumerian seal legends (31,512 records, 3,044 and 3,026) and Old Akkadian legends in Akkadian (89 records, 11 and 10). The frozen keep rule needs two corpora of each group with at least 25 eligible legends; only one of each entered, at threshold 25 and in the declared panel at 20, so no statistic was kept or rejected. Descriptively, at matched size 196 Indo-Aryan and Ur III separate in every draw: edge asymmetry +0.250 against -0.219, closing concentration 0.628 against 0.204, stock closure beyond shuffle +0.264 against -0.025, word-internal asymmetry +0.204 against -0.111; Tamil-Brahmi sits with Indo-Aryan at n = 18 (+0.363). The 11 Akkadian legends also end in few signs (edge asymmetry +0.134 beyond their shuffle range -0.073 to +0.092). An exploratory count after the runs puts titles before names in 57 of 61 Indo-Aryan pairs and after names in 2,393 of 2,475 Ur III pairs and 10 of 15 Akkadian pairs.

Twelve primary sources support sixteen source-located observations. Regional posturban occupation and practical retention coexist with marker changes, local abandonment and redistribution. In the Tamil Lexicon, compounds muruku-X and X-mīṉ share a member for 30.5% of 2,500 random replacement pairs (95% bootstrap 25.2-36.2%; 40.3% and 28.7% for pools of 25 and 100; 52.8% under the practised stem tolerance), so the frozen rule kills the veḷ interlock as evidence (threshold 20%). Four of five encoded interlocks hold for Parpola's words (veḷ, vaṭa-mīṉ, numeral-mīṉ compounds, katir-k-kaṭavuḷ; Muruka-p-piḷḷai is not in the Lexicon), and all four hold together in 0.44% of 10,000 random draws (2.2% under the practised tolerance), so the network passes the frozen 1% rule. Single homophones between 751 picturable nouns and 436 name meanings occur for 2.31% of evaluable pairs in DEDR, 1.50% in Turner's CDIAL and 0.45% in ePSD2; the Dravidian rate is 2.37 times the median and fails the frozen band of 0.5-2. Restricting each Tamil word to its own gloss lowers the Dravidian rate to 0.29%. Post-outcome: at Parpola's narrower search depth the veḷ link has a 7.8% chance rate; four successes among templates with mean chance rate 0.21 become likely once about 17 templates are tried; mīṉ forms star compounds with three, five, six and seven but not with two.

On 38 blind adjacent sign pairs (16 identified signs, pairs recurring in at least two distinct texts, published and already-examined pairs removed), Parpola's words form an attested two-member Tamil Lexicon compound for 9 pairs (23.7%) against 4.97 expected for matched random words (13.1%): ratio 1.81, 95% bootstrap interval 0.93-2.72, leave-one-out 1.64-1.98. P1 passes its frozen rule (ratio below 2; kill at 3 with lower bound above 1.5 not reached); 6.7% of random keys reach nine hits. Sensitivities give 1.56-2.42. Most hits pair his word with an unrelated homophone (veḷ-ḷ-āṉai 'white elephant' for āṉ 'cow'); iru-kaṇ 'two eyes' is the one apt reading. The hidden-member template (W1-X / X-W2) holds for 22 of 24 gapped pairs against 82% for random words (ratio 1.11). Parpola's twelve published pairs succeed seven times against 1.15 expected (ratio 6.1, 2.8-11.7). Post-outcome: published pairs succeed at 58% against 24% for blind pairs (one-sided Fisher p = 0.032); at the blind rate, seven successes become likely after about 28 tried pairs.

P2 failed under its frozen rule. Winslow has no two-member compound beginning with muruku (the Tamil Lexicon has 7) and 29 with mīṉ as last member (82), so replacement words matched on muruku's productivity have no compounds and none of 2,500 pairs shares a member (rate 0.0, Wilson 95% upper bound 0.15%; threshold above 0.20). Neither Muruka-vēḷ nor veṇ-mīṉ is a Winslow entry, so the veḷ interlock does not exist there; Skanda's name on vēḷ is cevvēḷ. Two of Parpola's five interlocks hold (vaṭa-mīṉ, aṟu-mīṉ) and random words reproduce both in 3.9% of 10,000 draws. Post-outcome: with pools matched to 7 first-member and 29 second-member compounds, random pairs share a member in 14.0% of cases in Winslow and 16.6% in the Lexicon; a complete parse would give muruku two first-member compounds (murukkam-pū, murukkañ-cettal), and pools matched to one compound give 2.8%.
